slides.title: Slide 5: AI's Impact on Professions
slides.narration: **AI** is not just a tool for fun; it is a major force changing the professional landscape across all industries.

slides.title: Slide 6: Automating vs. Augmenting Tasks
slides.narration: It is crucial to understand the difference between **AI** automation and augmentation.

slides.title: Slide 7: Automation
slides.narration:
Automation means **AI** takes over a repetitive task completely.
Think of it like a smart factory robot that does the same job perfectly every time.
For example, an **AI** system can automatically sort customer support emails.
It categorizes them into types like 'Billing' or 'Technical Issue'.

slides.title: Slide 8: Augmentation
slides.narration:
Augmentation, on the other hand, means **AI** acts as a partner.
It helps a human do their job better or faster.
This is where the biggest immediate impact is.
It is like having a helpful assistant who prepares everything for you.
For example, a marketing professional can use **AI** to brainstorm headlines. 
This can be done for an ad campaign in seconds. 
This allows them to focus their time on choosing and refining the best one.

slides.title: Slide 9: The Rise of New Job Roles
slides.narration:
**AI** is not just about changing old jobs; it is creating entirely new ones.
Let's look at some examples.

slides.title: Slide 10: Prompt Engineer
slides.narration:
One such new role is a **Prompt Engineer**. 
This is an expert who specializes in crafting the perfect **prompts**. 
Their goal is to get the most accurate results from **AI** models. 
They also aim for high-quality results from these models. 
These models include **ChatGPT** or **Gemini**.

slides.title: Slide 11: AI Auditor
slides.narration:
Another emerging role is an **AI Auditor**.
This professional tests and reviews **AI** systems to check for bias, ethical issues, and safety risks before they are released to the public.

slides.title: Slide 12: AI Content Manager
slides.narration:
We also have the **AI Content Manager**.
This person oversees the use of **AI** in content creation, ensuring that the **AI**-generated first drafts are fact-checked, edited, and refined to meet quality standards.

slides.title: Slide 13: How to Talk About AI Skills
slides.narration:
Simply listing '**ChatGPT**' on your resume is not enough.
You need to show how you use **AI** to create value.
Let's see how.

slides.title: Slide 14: Resume Example
slides.narration:
On your resume, focus on the results you achieved. 
Instead of writing: 'Proficient in **AI** tools.' 
Write this: 'Utilized **Google Gemini** to summarize complex research. 
This included various reports.' 
This action reduced content analysis time by 40%. 
Notice how the second example clearly states the tool used. 
It also states the task performed. 
It also highlights the measurable impact.

slides.title: Slide 15: Interview Example
slides.narration:
In an interview, frame **AI** as a productivity tool that enhances your skills. 
You could say: 'I see **AI** as a powerful assistant. 
I use it to handle first drafts and brainstorm ideas. 
This frees me up to spend more time on strategic thinking. 
It also allows for more time on editing and creative problem-solving.' 
This shows you understand **AI**'s role as an augmentation tool.

slides.title: Slide 16: Summary
slides.narration:
Let's summarize. 
In this tutorial, we learned that **AI** can automate repetitive tasks. 
It also augments human capabilities. 
We also learned that new job roles are emerging. 
Examples include **Prompt Engineer** and **AI Auditor**. 
Finally, we covered how to articulate **AI** skills on resumes. 
We also covered how to articulate them in interviews. 
This involves focusing on value and augmentation.

slides.title: Slide 17: Assignment
slides.narration:
Now, for a small activity.
Think of a task you do regularly at work or in your studies.
Describe how **AI** could either automate a part of it or augment your ability to perform it better.
Write down your thoughts.
